races.name: Ripon Racecourse Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (Special Rider Conditions)

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins in quick succession (last ran 3 days ago), all over shorter trips on soft/good ground, but sim-going score and hold-up style suits today; the step up to 1m4f after recent 10f wins is the key query, though Tony Carroll's prolific 14-day strike rate (7/62) underlines yard confidence.

runners_data.name: One Million Dreams
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has been running consistently at 10f-12f on Good ground and carries headgear; the 26-day break is manageable, but stepping up from 12f to 1m4f and a moderate sim-going score of 8/15 means this trip is not a certainty.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with five places from last five at similar distances on Good ground (10/15 sim-going), yet still to win in 15 comparable runs; Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form (9/104 14-day) and the trip and going pose no concerns.

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who races out of his natural role here (style fit 0.93), having won and placed on much slower surfaces with all career form on Standard; 83 days off and only 2/15 sim-going score on Good are real concerns, but his tactical advantage as lone leader cannot be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Held up off a 265-day absence (60 jumps runs during that time), but his two course wins at 1m4f+ on Good going (3W6P sim-going) make the return to this trip potentially ideal; the significant layoff is the single biggest risk.

runners_data.name: Bruce Banner
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with placed form at 12f-14f on Good going and two recent placings; a true hold-up horse whose position is shifted to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with closers, meaning the stylistic compromise is worth acknowledging even though his recent form profile is solid.

runners_data.name: Bouboule
runners_data.note: Has finished seventh in both Good-ground outings over today's trip at 1m4f+ and wears tongue strap; trainer has no 14-day runners to assess form, and with a 38-day break (11 jumps outings), the horse's natural hold-up style is compromised by the crowded back-of-field, where it must be repositioned on the map.

runners_data.name: Arranmore
runners_data.note: Regular prominent racer who has been running over shorter trips (8f-11f) recently and steps back up to 1m4f; wears cheekpieces/tongue strap, Micky Hammond yard in fair form (4/18), and showed two wins at 11f on Standard suggests this longer trip on Good ground is the unknown factor.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag and has a dismal recent record (no wins, largely mid-pack finishes on Standard); a genuine hold-up horse shifted to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, and Philip Kirby's yard has been quiet (0/22 14-day), making this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: One win from 14f on Standard and some placed efforts, but the hold-up style here is squeezed into a midfield position given the glut of closers; 16-day break, tongue strap, and a modest sim-going score of 5/15 on comparable going tempers enthusiasm despite the winning pedigree at this distance.

runners_data.name: Apache Eagle
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with placed form at 12f-14f on mostly Standard ground; shifted to midfield because of the crowded hold-up contingent, and with no wins in 15 sim-going runs (2/15) and an uninspiring recent form string of 327339, the case is limited despite the consistent placing.

runners_data.name: Yurinov
runners_data.note: Another Philip Kirby hold-up horse (yard 0/16 14-day), absent for 96 days and entirely reliant on Standard ground for all five recent runs (sim-going 3/15 on comparable); pushed from its natural rear position into a midfield slot, and the lack of any Good-ground recent evidence makes this a speculative runner at best.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse willing to lead, will face no meaningful pressure from the gates — settling into an uncontested, sustainable gallop on the Ripon 1m4f circuit. The hold-up dominated field means the pace will almost certainly be modest, with Langley able to control tempo and dictate the race from the front without being harried. Pride Of Nepal, One Million Dreams, Kitsune Power, and Max Of Stars are all genuine hold-up horses who will need to find plenty of room and momentum in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up finisher who can produce a sustained late run, provided the pace is genuine enough to set them alight — though the lone leader also holds a meaningful place chance if the tempo is too conservative to unwind the closers. This field contains far more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Bruce Banner, Bouboule, Speechman, Yakhabar, Apache Eagle, and Yurinov are all true hold-up horses pushed into the midfield graphic, and of those, Bruce Banner and Bouboule are best positioned to secure a workable tracking berth given their class and recent form.

scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley is allowed a soft, uncontested lead and the hold-up pack fails to generate a meaningful finishing surge.
scenarios.body: If Jack Langley is allowed a soft, uncontested lead and the hold-up pack fails to generate a meaningful finishing surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce Hard
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley's solo lead generates enough honest fractions to set up a strong final two furlongs for the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: If Jack Langley's solo lead generates enough honest fractions to set up a strong final two furlongs for the backmarkers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Arranmore tracks Langley closely and together they set a strong enough pace to stop the hold-up horses cold while grinding the field into submission.
scenarios.body: If Arranmore tracks Langley closely and together they set a strong enough pace to stop the hold-up horses cold while grinding the field into submission.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Ups Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the race fractures into a stop-start pace and the redistributed hold-up types — Bruce Banner and Bouboule — manage to secure a useful tracking position despite being pushed forward on the map.
scenarios.body: If the race fractures into a stop-start pace and the redistributed hold-up types — Bruce Banner and Bouboule — manage to secure a useful tracking position despite being pushed forward on the map.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Jack Langley is allowed to saunter in front unchallenged — if no horse moves to pressurise him in the first half mile, the race could be over turning for home.
Pride Of Nepal runs just 3 days after her last win; watch her in the paddock and in early running for signs of freshness or fatigue after a busy campaign.
Max Of Stars returns from a 265-day break having run on the jumps circuit; watch whether she settles and travels smoothly as an indicator of whether the layoff is inconsequential.

With six or more genuine hold-up types all wanting the back of the field, watch the early positioning battle — horses that get shuffled widest or furthest back from a poor draw or slow break will face a very significant task on the 1m4f Ripon track.

Arranmore is the most likely horse to move up and press Jack Langley after the first few furlongs; if she does, watch whether that shifts the race into Scenario C and changes the entire finishing order.

races.name: Live For Today Best Dressed Gentleman EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (B/C/D) (Qual') (GBB/IRE Inc')

runners_data.name: Pj's Corner
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha runner with a solo run of 8th over 7f on good ground; fades in the finish so a slow-burn sprint is less forgiving, but the step back to 6f could sharpen the finishing effort.|

runners_data.name: Super Alpha
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston two-year-old lightly raced after a 5th and 3rd at 5f — two runs suggest he is finding his feet; 53 days off is the notable flag, but Johnston is 7/50 in the 14-day window suggesting he readies horses between runs well.|

runners_data.name: Wong Fei Hong
runners_data.note: Debut runner for David O'Meara with no public form to assess; going and distance preferences unknown, and his style may only emerge from the stalls — the wild card if he shows natural pace.|

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 6th on debut over 5f on good ground; a natural hold-up horse that the congested field forces into a midfield berth, meaning he is racing slightly out of role — his style-fit of 0.90 should temper expectations unless the race collapses into a late dash.|

runners_data.name: Persazz
runners_data.note: William Knight debutant carrying top weight of 133lbs with no form lines; completely unknown quantity and could go any way, but the weight and unknown style make him a speculative entry in any scenario.|

runners_data.name: Printing Money
runners_data.note: Second Cunha runner alongside stablemate Pj's Corner — finished 9th over 6f on good ground last time out and is flagged as a horse who fades, which is a significant concern in a race likely to end in a sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Boutblummintime
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's Irish raider who has run 6th twice (6f good, 5f soft); his true hold-up nature is at odds with a crowded rear — he has been mapped to midfield to reflect the squeeze, and that positional compromise makes a bold showing harder to construct.|

runners_data.name: Carry On Chaos
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner who has finished 9th and 8th in two starts over 6f on good ground — he fades in the finish and is a genuine hold-up type forced into midfield by the weight of similar runners; Easterby is prolific (11/115 in 14 days) but this horse's profile is working against the likely race shape.|

runners_data.name: Inns And Out
runners_data.note: Second Easterby runner, finishing 5th on his sole start over 6f on good; David Allan takes the ride, and while the horse is a natural hold-up type displaced into midfield, Allan is an astute jockey who may manage the positional compromise better than most.|

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this Roger Fell debut runner with no public form; a stable that also runs Bigalo, so connections have a read on ability, but from a pace analysis standpoint he is an unknown who could influence tempo significantly.|

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's three-race juvenile has finished 7th, 5th and 8th across 5f and 6f on good ground — the most experienced horse by run-count in the field; 6 days since last run is tight but Lidster has no 14-day strike rate, and this horse's consistent form of mid-pack finishes suggests a modest ceiling.|

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 6f Ripon contest lacks a natural pace-setter and is likely to crawl early before degenerating into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. The majority of the field — Pj's Corner, Bigalo, Printing Money, Boutblummintime, Carry On Chaos, Inns And Out, and State Of Gold — are all hold-up types by profile, meaning nobody will want to make the running, and the pace will be manufactured rather than genuine. The three unknown-style debutants — Wong Fei Hong, Persazz, and Johns Power — could inadvertently inject early tempo if their handlers send them forward, but that remains speculative. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear; Boutblummintime, Carry On Chaos, and Inns And Out are most likely to be pushed into a midfield role against their natural instincts, while only Bigalo and State Of Gold may find genuine space off the pace. This race shape heavily favours horses who can travel smoothly in behind a falsely-run early pace and produce a sharp, decisive finish in the final furlong — a profile that suits any unexposed debutant with a natural turn of foot or a hold-up horse with strong closing form, rather than those who fade under sustained pressure.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a false start or a bunched break — with no natural front-runner among 11 runners, the first furlong could see chaotic jostling as nobody wants to lead, potentially causing interference and compromising hold-up horses like Bigalo and Inns And Out who cannot find their rhythm.

Persazz and Johns Power are both debutants carrying top weights and must be tracked from the gates — if either shows natural speed and bowls along in front, it completely reshapes the pace map and the scenario probabilities shift toward Scenario B.

Carry On Chaos and Boutblummintime are flagged as faders who are also being pushed out of their natural hold-up roles into midfield — if the pace is genuinely slow, both will find themselves trapped in a race shape that suits neither their instinct nor their finishing pattern.

Super Alpha's 53-day absence and Connor Beasley booking for Charlie Johnston is worth monitoring in the market — Johnston is 7/50 in 14 days suggesting horses are primed, and any significant market confidence for a horse with only two prior runs could signal a well-prepared return.|

State Of Gold ran just six days ago — the shortest turnaround in the field — and Craig Lidster has no recorded 14-day strike rate; monitor whether the horse moves freely in the paddock, as a quick reappearance on good ground after three unremarkable efforts could indicate either desperation for a qualification run or a perceived fitness peak.

races.name: Grantley Hall Handicap

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Johnston who has solid Good-ground form over this sort of trip, but sim-going record of 0 wins and 1 place from 15 runs on similar footing is modest; positioned late in a small field could leave her with too much to do if the pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and the key pace-setter, though his recent form of 6-7654 is poor and his sim-going record (2 from 15, 0W0P) on Good is a concern; tagged with a modest STYLE_FIT score indicating he is operating at the outer edge of his effective profile.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran for Easterby who has won twice on Good ground at around this trip in his last five runs, giving him the strongest sim-going profile in the race (2W3P from 10); prominent style suits the projected race shape perfectly and the headgear (p) is already applied.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Easterby pushed forward on the map because the field is stacked with rear-runners; his last five runs are all on softer surfaces with no wins on Good, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine caution against expecting his best here.

runners_data.name: What's The Plan
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old for Fanshawe who shaped with promise when third over 10f on Good and carries headgear (h); hold-up in profile but a small field may see the amateur-allowance claimer D'Arcy(7) have to make earlier moves than ideal, potentially bringing him into play.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: Consistent at the 3-placing level for O'Meara on similar ground, but his natural instinct is to race from the back and the redistribution to midfield means he will be asked to travel closer to the pace than he prefers; STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: The 2-year-old for Sir Mark Prescott returns from 182 days off with only three starts and all on Tapeta; completely unexposed on turf and on Good going, so his form reads as unknown quantity — Luke Morris is experienced enough to find him a position, but this race shape asks questions he has not yet answered.

races.paceDynamic: King Of Fury is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge him for the lead from the outset, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f Ripon trip on Good ground. Poet's Dawn will press from a prominent pitch behind him, but with King Of Fury uncontested, the pace is unlikely to be searingly strong — setting up a race where those tracking the leader in the first two or three positions hold a significant positional advantage at the top of the home straight. The field contains a cluster of true hold-up horses — Saxophonist, Roc De Fer, and Yermanthere — who cannot all settle at the rear in a seven-runner field and have been remapped to midfield, meaning they are racing out of their natural role and their finishing kicks may be compromised. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel smoothly just off a moderate pace and strike early in the home straight, rather than late-finishing hold-up types dependent on a tempo they are unlikely to get.

watchPoints.text: King Of Fury's willingness to stride on unchallenged is the pivotal factor — if he dwells or is slow away, the pace evaporates entirely and the race becomes a sprint finish from two furlongs, scrambling all projections.

Roc De Fer's 182-day absence combined with a switch from Tapeta to Good turf for the first time represents a significant unknown — Prescott horses can show up fresh but the form book offers no turf reading to anchor confidence.

Saxophonist, Roc De Fer, and Yermanthere are all natural hold-up horses compressed into a midfield role by field composition — monitor whether any of them drift back to their natural position in running, which would leave them needing a stronger pace than King Of Fury is likely to provide.

Poet's Dawn's record of 2 wins in last 5 on Good ground around this trip (10f) makes him the standout form pick for the projected race shape, and Tim Easterby's 14-day strike rate of 8/90 confirms the yard is in decent form to fire him in fresh off 6 days.

races.name: Ripon Races Ladies' Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Strong Warrior
runners_data.note: Richard Fahey's six-year-old is a hold-up type who fades in the finish — 132 days off is a concern and the flat 6f at Ripon on Good ground suits his best efforts, but he needs everything to fall right late and that record of fading suggests this pace shape may not be sharp enough to bring him into it.|

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has a strong trainer strike rate (10/60 over 14 days) and wears a visor; comfortable racing prominently, it has the profile to slot in behind Another Baar and make a forward move, though its form figures in Good-ground 6f races are inconsistent.|

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's six-year-old is the confirmed front-runner and carries a STYLE_FIT note at 0.93 indicating it is slightly out of role as a promoted prominent — on balance, it is still most likely to hold the lead, but the higher weight (135lbs) is worth noting at the business end of a handicap.|

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's hold-up specialist has winning course-and-distance form on Good ground and is the most credible closer in the field; 18 days since last run is fine, but Jason Hart will need a clear passage turning in and a genuine enough pace from Another Baar to bridge the gap.|

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old is a genuine prominent racer and Kevin Stott gives it every chance of securing a chasing position; it has been placed in five of its last five runs without winning, suggesting consistency without a killer change of gear — a straightforward prominent run could nonetheless see it fill a place.|

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old is a natural front-runner by inclination but is mapped to midfield here, squeezed out by more powerful prominent types — the tp headgear suggests a trainer trying to sharpen it up, yet racing out of its natural role at 0.93 style fit reduces its likelihood of landing a blow.|

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Another Easterby runner on a five-day turnaround, a true hold-up type repositioned to midfield on the map given the field's depth at the rear — its best recent effort came on Soft ground and the step up to Good at Ripon, combined with racing further forward than ideal, makes this a difficult task.|

races.paceDynamic: Another Baar is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Dark Cloud Rising and Wild Clary as genuine prominent types capable of applying pressure, the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching across this 6f Good-ground Ripon test. Another Baar can control from the front without being seriously harassed, setting a tempo that rewards horses who can travel in behind and pick up in the final two furlongs rather than those who need a true end-to-end gallop to deliver their finishing effort. Dark Thirty and Strong Warrior are the natural hold-up operators in the field, and with the pace honest but not fierce, the question becomes whether they can get close enough to the action turning for home. This race shape — a single front-runner dictating at a measured pace with modest pressure from a small band of chasers — most directly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce, though if the tempo is just right, a well-positioned hold-up horse with a clean run can still close. The field holds more prominent types than can all occupy their natural position; Dark Cloud Rising and Wild Clary are most likely to secure the main chasing slots, with Vince L'Amour forced to settle further back than it would prefer.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dark Cloud Rising or Wild Clary can secure a clean prominent position behind Another Baar — if both crowd the leader through the first two furlongs, the race risks getting scrappy and opening the door for Dark Thirty to close late.

Another Baar carries top weight (135lbs) and if it has left its effort behind from 12 days ago, the supposedly controlled front end could fade earlier than expected, collapsing the scenario that suits the field.

Dark Thirty's hold-up style requires traffic to part in the final furlong at Ripon — watch the draw and where Jason Hart finds himself entering the straight, as getting blocked could cost a horse with genuine winning form at this course and distance.

Strong Warrior has had 132 days off and the fade-in-finish flag is a persistent concern — if it shows early pace from the wide draw before weakening, it could disrupt the running of horses tracking through midfield.|

Vince L'Amour wearing tp (cheekpieces) for Tim Easterby is worth monitoring pre-race — if it jumps and forces its way into prominence naturally, it effectively changes the pace map and adds a second confirmed front-runner to a race currently built around one.|

races.name: Masons Gin 'Who Dares, Gins' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: The confirmed leader here, Kevin Stott takes over and Good ground is fine; her OR=63 is workable from the front but her recent form of 330-46 shows she is in a moderate vein and her style-fit score tempers confidence even if she does set the pace.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly returns quickly on 13 days' rest and wore a hood last time; a genuine hold-up operator whose true running style sits at the back of the field — placed into midfield only by necessity — so she needs a searching pace she is unlikely to get here.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Showed a useful second on Good ground in recent history and wears a visor, but her natural inclination to come from off the pace is compromised in a race where the tempo is set to be controlled; Joanna Mason will need to be creative with positioning.

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has the highest OR in the field at 65 and Connor Beasley rides; his hold-up style is natural rather than forced here, and his strong placed record on Good ground (2W3P) makes him a genuine player if he can find a run from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Wish This
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and won over 6f on Standard last time out, but Good ground form is thin; Alan Brown's yard is 0/4 in the 14-day window, and while his hold-up style is authentic, the lack of Good-ground wins is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Rajstar
runners_data.note: A long layoff of 124 days is the dominant concern here before any style discussion; Ben Haslam sends him out freshened and his only Good-ground run produced a 6th, so he faces a fitness question as well as a pace shape that will not naturally bring him into the race.

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's five-year-old returns from 72 days off with a yard that is 0/17 in the fortnight window — a blinking stat; his all-weather form on Standard surfaces dominates his history and Good turf is a genuinely unfamiliar context, sitting quietly at the back of the field in a race that will not wait for closers.

runners_data.name: Fircombe Hall
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's veteran has placed twice at 6f on both Good and Standard recently and races prominently, making him the most natural companion to Liosa up front; Cam Hardie knows the horse well and his course form (1/15 on Good at this track) is thin but his positional profile suits the race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Liosa is the one confirmed front runner here and, with Fircombe Hall also pressing forward from a prominent base, she is likely to lead into the straight at a sustainable rather than suicidal gallop on Good ground over six furlongs at Ripon. That measured pace sets up a race where the lead and prominent positions are the most valuable real estate, and neither is under serious threat from behind because the majority of the field are genuine hold-up types who will be racing off a tempo they cannot control. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than can realistically close from off the pace — Fan Mail, Big Apple Jack, Rajstar, and Federal Envoy are all true rear-of-field operators who have been mapped forward simply because the map has no room at the back, meaning their redistribution flatters the apparent pace contest. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: a controlled, uncontested pace from Liosa and Fircombe Hall strongly favours horses racing prominently or at worst tracking just behind the leaders, with closers carrying a structural disadvantage unless something goes wrong up front.

scenarios.body: If Liosa leads uncontested and Fircombe Hall tracks close, setting a fair but unhurried pace that rewards those on the bridle turning in.

scenarios.title: Fircombe Hall Takes Over
scenarios.trigger: If Liosa fades inside the final two furlongs and Fircombe Hall, who has strong placed form at 6f on Good ground, sweeps past to lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Unravels
scenarios.trigger: If the field gets fractious early or a slow start forces hold-up horses to choose between their natural style and covering the pace, causing positional scramble.
scenarios.body: If the field gets fractious early or a slow start forces hold-up horses to choose between their natural style and covering the pace, causing positional scramble.

watchPoints.text: Liosa vs Fircombe Hall — watch which of the two prominent types actually gets to the front at the break, as whichever leads uncontested holds the structural advantage throughout.

Mr Cool is the highest-rated horse in the field and Connor Beasley is an astute judge of pace; if he can sit just off the leaders rather than being swallowed by the redistribution traffic, he is the most dangerous closer here.

Fan Mail, Big Apple Jack, Rajstar and Federal Envoy are all bunched in midfield by redistribution rather than by choice — watch for a positional squeeze in the first furlong as four genuine hold-up horses and their riders negotiate who goes where.

Rajstar's 124-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — watch his market move in the final hour; Ben Haslam does place horses on returns but the yard's recent 14-day strike rate offers no reassurance.
Going has been consistent across all seven races at Ripon today, all returning Good — no deterioration expected, so no runner gains a late ground advantage from conditions changing through the card.

races.name: Your Harrogate Ladies' Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the race, she makes the running from the front and on good ground over a mile is the key race-shaper; Tim Easterby in strong form (10/103 14-day) and David Allan aboard, though her style fit note (0.93) reflects she is placed slightly out of role here — her chance depends on whether she can convert a lone lead into a winning performance.

runners_data.name: Lc Tiffen
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type racing off a 19-day break for a yard without a recent winner (0/4 14-day); has struggled to place on good ground in five recent starts (0W0P) but the step up to a mile is unexplored territory that could suit her staying profile if the race develops with cut and thrust.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Spirit
runners_data.note: Back after 66 days off for Nigel Tinkler, who has had no winners in 13 runs over 14 days — the fitness question is real; has finished fourth or better in her last three starts but predominantly on soft/standard, and good ground represents only 1 from 4 similar-conditions runs.

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: The standout form angle — a winner 10 days ago over 7f on good and placed seven times in 15 good-ground starts (1W1P in similar going); Tony Carroll sends one over (7/47 14-day) and Kieren Fox's claim helps, making her the most consistent handicapper in this field.

runners_data.name: Raven's View
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural race position is at the rear of the field — placed at midfield on the map only because this race is overloaded with closers; has been beaten into the frame just once in six good-ground runs and has shown headgear (p) without success, which tempers optimism for Connor Beasley.

runners_data.name: A Boy Named Mary
runners_data.note: Carries a tagged warning for fading in finishes, which is a structural concern in a race where his true hold-up style gets redistributed to midfield — form figures of 407-08 are uninspiring and Nigel Tinkler's yard is cold over 14 days (6/25); the combination of style-fit discount and fade flag makes him hard to rely on.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: The sole winner in this field over the exact trip and going combination (1 win, 2 places from 8 good-ground runs at a mile); Tim Easterby's other runner and Sean Kirrane claims 3lbs — his most recent run was a third and his form profile is the most convincing of the redistributed hold-up horses despite being mapped to midfield due to field congestion at the rear.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Has been placed four times but is yet to win, and wears a visor for Joanna Mason and the Michael & David Easterby yard (2/28 14-day); good ground suits (4 from 11 similar-conditions runs in the frame) and the mile trip has produced her best finishes, though she remains a place proposition rather than a winner.

runners_data.name: Regal Knight
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes over for Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood (0/12 14-day) on a horse who has been placed four times from six good-ground runs but always behind the winner; the step back to a mile from longer trips in recent runs is interesting, though his redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up style and a cold yard reduces confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Hatamoto is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap at Ripon and is expected to bowl along in front at a comfortable, uncontested gallop on good ground — there is nothing to push her off her rhythm or force a punishing tempo. With no genuine challenger for the lead, the pace is likely to be honest rather than fierce, setting up a race where horses travelling prominently behind the leader are ideally positioned to pounce entering the straight. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically race at the rear — Raven's View, A Boy Named Mary, Hood Wink, Trucial Pearl and Regal Knight are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the genuine back-of-the-field option is more congested than it appears, and those with the lowest draw or sharpest acceleration will be best placed. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone front-runner setting a sustainable pace on a flat, fair track favours horses racing prominently or in a close-chasing position — those who can sit second or third without covering extra ground and produce a clean run into the straight.

watchPoints.text: Watch Shes Got The Blues to track the pace from a prominent position — if she gets a good run through into second or third early, her recent winning form on good ground and consistent place record make her the most dangerous closer in the race.

Hood Wink must find clear air from midfield in the straight; if he gets blocked behind a wall of redistributed hold-up horses all racing out of position, his proven winning profile at a mile on good goes to waste — watch his early move for daylight at the two-furlong pole.

Hatamoto's gallop rate in the first half-mile will define the entire race shape — if she dawdles and the field concertinas, the race becomes a sprint finish that neutralises her positional advantage and opens the door for closers.

A Boy Named Mary's fade flag combined with Shimmering Spirit's 66-day absence means two of the nine runners carry fitness or stamina doubts — both are likely to be outpaced in the final furlong if the pace quickens, and neither should be trusted in accumulators or combination bets.

With five horses genuinely competing for hold-up slots at the rear, traffic management in the straight at Ripon's one-mile course will be critical — horses with the widest draw or jockeys most willing to switch outside (Beasley on Raven's View, Hart on Regal Knight) may gain a marginal passage advantage.
